news.title: Leandro Paredes involved in another controversial moment weeks after World Cup brawl
news.lede: Leandro Paredes has caught the headlines again for all the wrong reasons. Following the FIFA World Cup 2026 Final in which Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, USA, the defender ended up in a scuffle in which he seemingly grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat before launching Gavi towards the ground. And now he’s back in hot water. On August 2, Boca Juniors travelled to Estadio Marcelo Bielsa in Rosario, Argentina, to take on Newell’s Old Boys in an Argentine Primera Division fixture.

news.title: Gianni Infantino opponents 'plotting rival World Cup competition' to 'paralyse' Fifa until he quits
news.lede: UEFA has joined forces with other confederations and threatened to set up their own version of the World Cup if disgraced Fifa supremo Gianni Infantino refuses to quit. The Swiss millionaire, 56, sensationally vowed to desperately cling onto his job after sending shockwaves through football. Infantino made shock plans to flog shares in the World Cup to private investors before being forced into a humiliating U-turn. And Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin, along with Concacaf and Asian Football Confederation chiefs, is pushing for him to resign.

news.title: Radio presenters were 1966 World Cup heroes too
news.lede: Andrew Keeley will never forget Brian Moore and Alan Clarke’s commentary on BBC radio. Garry Richardson (England’s 1966 World Cup heroes were fun, humble and unlike today’s stars, 30 July) appears to make the assumption that everyone watched the 1966 World Cup final on television with Kenneth Wolstenholme’s iconic commentary. As a football-mad 10-year-old, I had the misfortune on the day of the final to be on our family summer holiday in the then sleepy village of Goathland, staying in a house with no TV. Hope rose when my dad was invited to watch the final at a neighbour’s who had one of the few TVs in the village and he asked if he could bring his children.

news.title: UEFA warns FIFA of legal action over Infantino's failed plan to sell the World Cup
news.lede: "The UEFA, the governing body of European football, threatened FIFA with taking legal action over Gianni Infantino's failed plan to sell a stake in future World Cup profits to private investors, and said that no potential evidence should be destroyed. The proposal, kept secret by Infantino to raise $4.2 billion from investors, including Joshua Kushner's New York investment firm, was abandoned early on Saturday, days after its revelation in press reports caused a global uproar. 'UEFA led the reaction and on Thursday its 55 member associations met to agree to boycott all FIFA events and competitions while the proposal remained in force.

news.title: UEFA declare loss of confidence in Infantino after World Cup sell-off controversy
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. FIFA president Gianni Infantino has “lost the confidence” of UEFA over a plan to sell stakes in a World Cup company to private investors, the European football governing body has said. Infantino announced overnight that the plan would not proceed after three confederations rejected it, with UEFA going further and saying it would boycott FIFA competitions until the proposal was scrapped.

news.title: UEFA considering legal action against FIFA prez Infantino over World Cup sell-off plan
news.lede: UEFA is considering legal action against FIFA president Gianni Infantino. The European football body warned Infantino not to destroy World Cup sell-off plan documents. This proposal involved private investment and faced widespread criticism from football organizations. UEFA and other confederations expressed strong opposition to the controversial plan.
